topic.topic: Base rates and the false positive paradox
topic.angle: Natural frequencies: count 1,000 drivers instead of juggling percentages

card.title: Why a positive test is probably wrong

body.question: A breathalyzer wrongly flags 5% of sober drivers and never misses a drunk one. One driver in 1,000 is drunk. A random driver tests positive. How likely is it that they are drunk?
body.reveal: About 2%. Picture 1,000 drivers: 1 is drunk and tests positive, while about 50 of the 999 sober drivers test positive too. So only around 1 positive in 51 is real. When something is rare, false alarms from the many outnumber true hits from the few.

probes.question: True or false: when a condition is very rare, most positive results can still be false positives.
Besides a test's accuracy, what else decides how much a positive result means?
options: How common the condition is in the people tested
How many tests were run last year

claims.claim: Breathalyzer wrongly flags 5% of sober drivers
claims.quote: Imagine that a group of police officers have breathalyzers displaying false drunkenness in 5% of the cases in which the driver is sober

claims.claim: Never misses a drunk driver; one in 1,000 drivers is drunk
claims.quote: the breathalyzers never fail to detect a truly drunk person. One in a thousand drivers is driving drunk.

claims.claim: Correct probability of being drunk after a positive test is about 2%, not 95%
claims.quote: Many would estimate the probability that the driver is drunk as high as 95%, but the correct probability is about 2%.

claims.claim: Of 1,000 drivers 1 drunk true positive, about 50 of 999 sober false positives, about 1 in 51
claims.quote: 999 drivers are not drunk, and among those drivers there are 5% false positive test results, so there are 49.95 false positive test results

claims.claim: Probe: when a condition is very rare, most positives can still be false (true)
claims.quote: This paradox describes situations where there are more false positive test results than true positives

claims.claim: Probe: how common the condition is (base rate) also decides what a positive means
claims.quote: is a type of fallacy in which people tend to ignore the base rate
